This code prepares the spatial data for the Gulf of California region. For the equal area projections, I will use Albers Equal Area EPSG:5070

Area of the GoC: 179,938 km2 (177,000 km2 according to [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_California))

```{r setup, include=FALSE, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(magrittr)
library(mregions2)
library(mapview)
library(sf)
library(tidyverse)
library(lwgeom)
library(here)
library(leaflet.extras2)
library(terra)

# this CRS might be better for visualization, explore.
gulf_crs <- "+proj=aea +lat_1=23 +lat_2=30 +lat_0=25 +lon_0=-110 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"

```

*STEP 1* Obtain high resolution polygon of Gulf of California region

Open Street Map has the highest resolution coastline data. Data downloaded from here (Dec 18 2024): <https://osmdata.openstreetmap.de/data/water-polygons.html>

Combined with data from: <https://www.marineregions.org/downloads.php> to get border data.

*STEP 2* Make some decisions

### Question 1: Should we follow the Gulf of California political boundary? Or, should we follow the Ecoregion boundary?

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, results="hide", eval=FALSE}

coastline <- st_read("/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/spatial/water-polygons-split-4326/water_polygons.shp")

# select the ones relevant to Gulf of California
# mapview(coastline[1:2000,]) #figure out how the data are arranged
valids <- st_is_valid(coastline)
coastline_valid <- coastline[valids, ] # some not valid, but not any I care about.

bbox <- c(xmin=-118.4, ymin = 14.55, xmax = -86.739, ymax = 32.718) # Mexico boundaries
coastline_mexico <- st_crop(coastline_valid, bbox)
#mapview(coastline_mexico) +
#mapview(joined_mexico, col="red")

# further crop
GoC <- coastline_mexico[c(37, 164, 187, 112, 32, 237, 3, 70, 234, 39, 31, 65, 142,
                          254, 157, 461, 202, 143, 66, 248, 159, 62, 139,
                          82, 33, 84, 241, 243, 64, 412, 136, 123, 168, 393,
                          394, 79, 140, 182, 90, 378, 377, 376, 360, 361, 362, 363,  60, 169, 161, 137, 
                          124, 242, 245, 246, 55, 56, 59, 63, 249, 113),]
#mapview(GoC, col.regions="red") + 
#  mapview(coastline_mexico, col.regions="blue")

## join these polygons together
joined_mexico <- st_union(GoC)
joined_mexico <- st_sf(geometry = joined_mexico)
#mapview(joined_mexico)

## map 1: based on Gulf of Mexico boundary
iho_mexico <- mrp_get("iho") %>%
  filter(name == "Gulf of California")
#mapview(iho_mexico)

## map 2: based on ecoregion boundary
eco_mexico <- mrp_get("ecoregions") %>%
  filter(ecoregion == "Cortezian")
#mapview(eco_mexico)

#couldn't get clip to work, so had to draw lines by hand based on references

#eco
eco_line_coords <- matrix(c(
  -110.00083, 22.85750,  # Start point (x1, y1)
   -105.68781, 20.41197   # End point (x2, y2)
), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)

# Create the LINESTRING geometry
eco_line <- st_sfc(st_linestring(eco_line_coords), crs = 4326)
eco_line <- st_sf(geometry = eco_line)
#mapview(eco_line, color="red")+
#mapview(eco_mexico)
#mapview(eco_line, color="red")+
#mapview(joined_mexico)

eco_line <- st_geometry(eco_line)

eco_hr <- st_split(joined_mexico, eco_line)
eco_hr <- st_collection_extract(eco_hr, "POLYGON")
eco_hr <- eco_hr[1,]
eco_hr <- st_sf(geometry = eco_hr)

#mapview(eco_hr)
st_write(eco_hr, here("spatial/GoC_polygon_ecoregion_latlon.shp"), append=FALSE, quiet=TRUE)
eco_hr_equal_area <- st_transform(eco_hr, 5070)
st_write(eco_hr_equal_area, here("spatial/GoC_polygon_ecoregion_eqarea.shp"), append=FALSE, quiet=TRUE)
```


```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
## make 1km resolution raster from each dataset.
bbox <- st_bbox(eco_hr_equal_area)
r <- rast(
  xmin = bbox["xmin"], xmax = bbox["xmax"],
  ymin = bbox["ymin"], ymax = bbox["ymax"],
  resolution = 1000,  # 1 km resolution
  crs = st_crs(eco_hr_equal_area)$proj4string  # Use the same CRS as your polygon
)

# Convert the sf object to a terra SpatVector
eco_shape <- vect(eco_hr_equal_area)

# Rasterize the polygon by fraction of cell covered
eco_rast <- rasterize(eco_shape, r, field = NA, touches = FALSE, cover = TRUE)
writeRaster(eco_rast, here("spatial/eco_raster_eqarea.tif"), overwrite=TRUE)

# Convert the sf object to a terra SpatVector
iho_shape <- vect(iho_hr_equal_area)

# Rasterize the polygon by fraction of cell covered
iho_rast <- rasterize(iho_shape, r, field = NA, touches = FALSE, cover = TRUE)
writeRaster(iho_rast, here("spatial/iho_raster_eqarea.tif"), overwrite=TRUE)
```

### Question 2: Should we include subregions?

Should we have one OHI score that represents the entire region? We can make further divisions according to ecoregions, estados, etc. The region is fairly small, so I'm not convinced subdivision makes sense.

This image provides estados and ecoregions boundaries:

![](images/GoC_estados.jpeg)

This image provides ecoregion boundaries: ![](images/GoC_ecoregions.jpeg) This image provides a useful view of the primary river inputs (for reference): ![](images/GoC_rivers.jpeg)

## Updated regions

### Inland boundary

Use inland watershed boundaries for now! We can decide from there.

Use Faro de Cabo Corrientes as the southeastern boundary, dart up the continental shelf, and connect to Cabo del Este southwestern boundary.

```{r}
# read in watersheds from mexico
watersheds_mexico <- st_read(here("/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/spatial/Major Watersheds of Mexico/data/commondata/data0/MEXICO_allbasins_Diss_Lambert.shp")) # CRS = North_America_Lambert_Conformal_Conic
mapview(watersheds_mexico)

# reproject to WGS 84 to align with mapview
watersheds_mexico_reproj <- st_transform(watersheds_mexico, st_crs(eco_hr))
# mapview(watersheds_mexico_reproj)
```

![](images/hem_watersheds_red_counties_blue.png)

The image is located [here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1m-cYhNwUm9I_iaC2oXYJDUAIVvi--2HLPQhiEDwwxf4/edit?tab=t.mg1p6em671r2).

Here we can see that the watersheds from databasin actually do not look very similar to the watersheds from Hem's data, which makes me think they may be using different ways to delineate between watersheds. Or that Hem's is more updated. Example: the tip of the peninsula by La Paz looks very different and much more segmented in the watersheds_mexico_proj.

Let's look at one from INEGI:

Theme: Hydrography State: United Mexican States Edition: 2006 Format: Electronic Scale: 1:250,000 Date: ITRF92

THE DIGITAL HYDROGRAPHIC NETWORK OF MEXICO SCALE 1:250 000, Edition 1.0. It is the result of connecting and giving logical sense according to the topography, rivers, streams, canals and aqueducts; the procedure consists of generating, by automated and semi-automated means, the continuity in the trace from the source of a water current to its mouth to the sea, inland body of water or when it disappears due to some process of infiltration into the subsoil. The drainage network is basically defined as a system of channels through which surface and subsurface runoff flows temporarily or permanently. Its importance is manifested by its effects on the formation and drainage speed of normal or extraordinary runoff; in addition to providing clues about the physical conditions of the soils, the surface and morphometry of the basin. Types of current and magnitude of order within a basin. Therefore, currents are commonly classified into; perennial and intermittent; This is based on the consistency of their runoff or flow, which is related to the physical and climatic characteristics of the basin. Perennial streams carry water all the time, except during extreme droughts. An intermittent stream carries water most of the time, but primarily during the rainy season. The hydraulic infrastructure works that allow the continuity of the Hydrographic Network considered in this work are canals and aqueducts.

```{r}
mapview(intersection_goc_cuencas_subrgns)
```

Okay, so it looks like we will need to include a buffer to ensure that all watersheds are included. I thought this buffer should be 1km, as that was mentioned in EWG #1 as a possible border.

```{r}
# for distance calculations, transform to UTM (32611 for Baja California)
subregion_proj_utm <- st_transform(subregion_draft_2_valid, crs = 32611) # UTM Zone 11N
cuencas_proj_utm <- st_transform(cuencas_hidrografica_2007_valid, crs = 32611)

# make a 1km buffer, aka 1000m
subregion_buffered <- st_buffer(subregion_proj_utm, dist = 1000)
mapview(subregion_buffered)

# intersect with the buffered polygons for the subregions
cuencas_within_1km <- st_intersection(cuencas_proj_utm, subregion_buffered)
mapview(cuencas_within_1km)

cov_id_cuencas_within_1km <- cuencas_within_1km$COV_ID

# filter the watershed dataset for all watersheds that are present in the intersection.
cuencas_surrounding_goc <- cuencas_proj_utm %>% 
  filter(COV_ID %in% cov_id_cuencas_within_1km)
mapview(cuencas_surrounding_goc)
```

Now, let's join the bordering watersheds to the subregion draft to create a full study area draft.

```{r}
# keep the individual cuenca polygons but add subregion information to each one
cuencas_surrounding_goc_w_rgns <- st_join(cuencas_surrounding_goc_clean, subregion_buffered) 
mapview(cuencas_surrounding_goc_w_rgns, zcol = "rgn_n_2")

full_study_area_draft <- bind_rows(cuencas_surrounding_goc_w_rgns, subregion_proj_utm) %>% 
  mutate(rgn_n_2 = factor(
    rgn_n_2,
    levels = paste0("Region_", sort(as.numeric(gsub("Region_", "", unique(rgn_n_2)))))
  ))
mapview(full_study_area_draft, zcol = "rgn_n_2")

# save it to mazu!
st_write(full_study_area_draft, here("/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/spatial/subregions_drafts/june_24", "full_study_area_draft_w_watersheds_utm.shp"))

# merge all polygons that fall in the same regions together
cuencas_surrounding_goc_by_rgn <- cuencas_surrounding_goc_w_rgns %>% 
  group_by(rgn_n_2) %>% 
  summarise(geometry = st_union(geometry), .groups = "drop") # merge the geometries
mapview(cuencas_surrounding_goc_by_rgn)

full_study_area_draft_merged <- bind_rows(cuencas_surrounding_goc_by_rgn, subregion_proj_utm) %>% 
  mutate(rgn_n_2 = factor(
    rgn_n_2,
    levels = paste0("Region_", sort(as.numeric(gsub("Region_", "", unique(rgn_n_2)))))
  ))
mapview(full_study_area_draft_merged, zcol = "rgn_n_2")
```

### Subregion drafting

Editing the ecoregion boundary to have a more accurate outline border.

```{r}
library(mapedit)
library(tidyverse)

eco_hr_foredit <- st_read(here("spatial/GoC_polygon_ecoregion_latlon.shp")) # WGS 84

# edit the polygon interactively
eco_hr_foredit_interactive <- editFeatures(eco_hr_foredit)
st_write(eco_hr_foredit_interactive, here("spatial/eco_hr_subregions_raw.shp"))

mapview(eco_hr_foredit_interactive)

##########################
# keep re-adding any lines that did were not valid
# edit interactively
eco_hr_polygon_subregions_03 <- editFeatures(eco_hr_polygon_subregions_02)
mapview(eco_hr_polygon_subregions_03)
st_write(eco_hr_polygon_subregions, here("spatial/eco_hr_subregions_raw.shp"))
##########################

## now merge polylines and split the original polygon with the new lines made

# original single GoC polygon
original_goc <- subregions_02

# polygon with mapedit lines
drawn_features <- eco_hr_polygon_subregions_03

# first extract only the lines (not the filled polygons) to see them and confirm
lines_only <- drawn_features[st_geometry_type(drawn_features) == "LINESTRING", ]

if(nrow(lines_only) == 0) {
  # Convert polygon boundaries to lines
  polygon_boundaries <- st_cast(drawn_features, "MULTILINESTRING")
  lines_only <- st_cast(polygon_boundaries, "LINESTRING")
}

mapview(lines_only)

# now use st_split to divide the original polygon into multiple polygons using the drawn lines
split_goc_with_lines <- function(original_polygon, dividing_lines) {

  # combine all lines into a single multilinestring
  all_lines <- st_union(st_geometry(dividing_lines))

  # split the original polygon
  tryCatch({
    split_result <- st_split(original_polygon, all_lines)

    # extract individual polygons from the result
    individual_polygons <- st_collection_extract(split_result, "POLYGON")

    # add region identifiers
    individual_polygons$region_id <- 1:nrow(individual_polygons)
    individual_polygons$region_name <- paste0("Region_", individual_polygons$region_id)

    return(individual_polygons)

  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Error in splitting:", e$message, "\n")
    cat("Trying alternative approach...\n")
    return(NULL) # for error catching!!
  })
}

# apply the splitting
subregions_03 <- split_goc_with_lines(original_goc, lines_only)
mapview(subregions_03)

region_7 <- subregions_03 %>% 
  filter(region_id == "9") # small polygon!!! needs to be merged...

mapview(region_7)

# drop the polygons for the southern border that are unnecessary and merge region 14 and 15. Also merge region 9 with region 8
merge_southern_border <- subregions_03 %>% 
  filter(!region_id %in% c("1", "16", "2")) %>% 
  mutate(region_id = ifelse(region_id == "15", "14", region_id)) %>%  # give it the same ID to merge 
  mutate(region_id = ifelse(region_id == "9", "8", region_id)) %>%
  group_by(region_id) %>%
  summarise(geometry = st_union(geometry), .groups = "drop") # merge the geometries

cleaned_subregions <- merge_southern_border %>% 
  arrange(as.numeric(region_id)) %>%  
  mutate(
    new_id = row_number(),
    region_id = as.character(new_id),
    region_name = paste0("Region_", new_id)
  )

# save it!!
st_write(cleaned_subregions, here("/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/spatial/subregions_drafts/june_24", "goc_subregions_draft.shp"), append = FALSE)
st_write(cleaned_subregions, here("spatial/goc_subregions_draft.shp"), append = FALSE)

mapview(cleaned_subregions, zcol = "region_name", layer.name = "Subregions") # looks great!!!
```

### Recoding POEM Rgns

#### Draft 1 (with 11 subregions)

##### Colors by OHI rgns

```{r}
# read in valid poem areas to use
poem_valid <- st_read(here("/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/spatial/subregions_drafts/poem","poem_valid.shp"))

# make new_FID_rgn column based on FID_1 values that fit into the possible 11 OHI subregions
poem_subrgns_ohi <- poem_valid %>%
  mutate(
    new_FID_rgn = case_when(
      FID_1 %in% c("2", "1") ~ "Region_1",
```

```{r}
# ##########################

## now merge polylines and split the original polygon with the new lines made

# original single GoC polygon
original_goc <- poem_subrgns_ohi_draft2

# polygon with mapedit lines
drawn_features <- poem_subrgns_ohi_draft2_01

# first extract only the lines (not the filled polygons) to see them and confirm
lines_only <- drawn_features[st_geometry_type(drawn_features) == "LINESTRING", ]

if(nrow(lines_only) == 0) {
  # make polygon boundaries into lines
  polygon_boundaries <- st_cast(drawn_features, "MULTILINESTRING")
  lines_only <- st_cast(polygon_boundaries, "LINESTRING")
}

mapview(lines_only)

# now use st_split to divide the original polygon into multiple polygons using the drawn lines
split_goc_with_lines <- function(original_polygon, dividing_lines) {

  # combine all lines into a single multilinestring
  all_lines <- st_union(st_geometry(dividing_lines))

  # split the original polygon
  tryCatch({
    split_result <- st_split(original_polygon, all_lines)

    # extract individual polygons from the result
    individual_polygons <- st_collection_extract(split_result, "POLYGON")

    # add region identifiers
    individual_polygons$nw_FID_ <- 1:nrow(individual_polygons)
    individual_polygons$region_name <- paste0("Region_", individual_polygons$nw_FID_)

    return(individual_polygons)

  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Error in splitting:", e$message, "\n")
    cat("Trying alternative approach...\n")
    return(NULL) # for error catching!!
  })
}

# apply the splitting
poem_subrgns_ohi_draft4 <- split_goc_with_lines(original_goc, lines_only)
mapview(poem_subrgns_ohi_draft4)
```

#### Draft 3 (9 subregions, Jorge's edits)

As a recap, technically this new draft will be shown to the EWG as Draft #2.  However, upon receiving Jorge's most recent comments (will paste them below), we decided to make these changes: 

(1) Change the border of Region_1 and Region_5 to include San Felipe and Puerto Penasco within those regions.  Before, those two cities were in Region_2 and Region_6.  But Jorge felt it makes the most sense to include the entire city in the upper gulf ecoregion.

(2) Add POEM region #61 and #71 into Region_3. **(Scratch that. ACTUALLY, we are keeping them in Region_4, as Ben W. said Punta San Antonio is best. So, no changes here.)**

(3) Alter the present POEM region that borders Region_6 and Region_7 to be just north of El Choyudo, so that Tastiota is within Region_6, but the entirety of El Choyudo is within Region_7. This is important because Tastiota has shrimp farming and should all be in one region, and just north of El Choyudo marks a change in the plant species composition/terrain (becomes more elevated).  This also follows the geologic map of Scott E. K. Bennett in the textbook shared with us by Ben W. (<https://www.desertfoodplants.org/_files/ugd/d133c2_7bdc031c4f9c4dbf9907de20f1944079.pdf>).

Okay! To do this, we will draw the new borders for Region_1, Region_5, and Region_6/7, and then use those lines to split the polygons.  Then instead of merging the new polygons created in the Regions_1/5 with the appropriate present POEM regions, we will just have two columns:

-  "POEM_id": where the newly split polygons will have the same ID as the one they split from. Aka, both will be "0"
-  "POEM_modified": where each polygon will have a unique name. Aka, polygon "0a" and "0b".

These will then be reclassified again to fit into OHI subregions (Regions 1-9), and then those will be reclassified to fit into states and ecoregions.


##### Map edit

Make lines:
```{r}
library(mapedit)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(here)
library(lwgeom)

# use mapedit to create the changes in the previous draft

draft_2_foredit <- st_read(here("/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/spatial/subregions_drafts/poem_w_ohi_draft","poem_subrgns_ohi_9rgns_final.shp")) # WGS 84

# edit the polygon interactively
draft_3_edited_w_lines <- editFeatures(draft_2_foredit)
# st_write(poem_subrgns_ohi_draft2_01, here("spatial/poem_subrgns_ohi_draft2_01.shp"))

mapview(draft_3_edited_w_lines)
```

Use lines to split polygons:
```{r}
## now merge polylines and split the original polygon with the new lines made

# original single GoC polygon
original_goc <- draft_2_foredit

# load the polygon with lines from mapedit
drawn_features <- draft_3_edited_w_lines

# first extract only the lines (not the filled polygons) to see them and confirm
lines_only <- drawn_features[st_geometry_type(drawn_features) == "LINESTRING", ]

if(nrow(lines_only) == 0) {
  # make polygon boundaries into lines
  polygon_boundaries <- st_cast(drawn_features, "MULTILINESTRING")
  lines_only <- st_cast(polygon_boundaries, "LINESTRING")
}

mapview(lines_only)

# now use st_split to divide the original polygon into multiple polygons using the drawn lines
split_goc_with_lines <- function(original_polygon, dividing_lines) {

  # combine all lines into a single multilinestring
  all_lines <- st_union(st_geometry(dividing_lines))

  # split the original polygon
  tryCatch({
    split_result <- st_split(original_polygon, all_lines)

    # extract individual polygons from the result for geometry
    individual_polygons <- st_collection_extract(split_result, "POLYGON")

    # add region identifiers (POEM_modified so that each one has its own identifier)
    individual_polygons$POEM_modified <- 1:nrow(individual_polygons)
    # individual_polygons$region_name <- paste0("Region_", individual_polygons$POEM_modified)

    return(individual_polygons)

  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Error in splitting:", e$message, "\n")
    cat("Trying alternative approach...\n")
    return(NULL) # for error catching!!
  })
}

# apply the splitting
draft_3_edited_polygons <- split_goc_with_lines(original_goc, lines_only)
```

##### Map edit

Make lines:
```{r}
library(mapedit)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(here)
library(lwgeom)

# use mapedit to create the changes in the previous draft

draft_3_foredit <- st_read(here("/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/spatial/subregions_drafts/poem_w_ohi_draft2","poem_ohi_draft2_070825_final.shp")) # WGS 84

# edit the polygon interactively
draft_4_edited_w_lines <- editFeatures(draft_3_foredit)
# st_write(poem_subrgns_ohi_draft2_01, here("spatial/poem_subrgns_ohi_draft2_01.shp"))

mapview(draft_4_edited_w_lines)
```

Use lines to split polygons:
```{r}
## now merge polylines and split the original polygon with the new lines made

# original single GoC polygon
original_goc <- draft_3_foredit

# load the polygon with lines from mapedit
drawn_features <- draft_4_edited_w_lines

# first extract only the lines (not the filled polygons) to see them and confirm
lines_only <- drawn_features[st_geometry_type(drawn_features) == "LINESTRING", ]

if(nrow(lines_only) == 0) {
  # make polygon boundaries into lines
  polygon_boundaries <- st_cast(drawn_features, "MULTILINESTRING")
  lines_only <- st_cast(polygon_boundaries, "LINESTRING")
}

mapview(lines_only)

# now use st_split to divide the original polygon into multiple polygons using the drawn lines
split_goc_with_lines <- function(original_polygon, dividing_lines) {

  # combine all lines into a single multilinestring
  all_lines <- st_union(st_geometry(dividing_lines))

  # split the original polygon
  tryCatch({
    split_result <- st_split(original_polygon, all_lines)

    # extract individual polygons from the result for geometry
    individual_polygons <- st_collection_extract(split_result, "POLYGON")

    # add region identifiers (POEM_modified so that each one has its own identifier)
    individual_polygons$POEM_modified <- 1:nrow(individual_polygons)
    # individual_polygons$region_name <- paste0("Region_", individual_polygons$POEM_modified)

    return(individual_polygons)

  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Error in splitting:", e$message, "\n")
    cat("Trying alternative approach...\n")
    return(NULL) # for error catching!!
  })
}

# apply the splitting
draft_4_edited_polygons <- split_goc_with_lines(original_goc, lines_only)
mapview(draft_4_edited_polygons)

# to see what needs to be changed
draft_4_ids <- draft_4_edited_polygons %>% 
  # select(FID_1, p_mod, POEM_modified) %>% # only used for creating the case_when
  mutate(p_mod_2 = case_when ( # the ones with "a" are the original poly it split from, "b" are the ones we made
    POEM_modified %in% "3" ~ "1b", # Rgn_1 new bottom poly
    POEM_modified %in% "4" ~ "1a", # Rgn_1 origin for new bottom poly
    POEM_modified %in% "5" ~ "2b", # Rgn_1 new top poly (closer)
    POEM_modified %in% "6" ~ "2a", # Rgn_1 origin for new top poly
    POEM_modified %in% "77" ~ "70b", # going to pta. mercenario (poly closest to shore)
    POEM_modified %in% "78" ~ "70a", # going to pta. mercenario (poly closest to shore)
    POEM_modified %in% "66" ~ "60a", # going to pta. mercenario (middle poly)
    POEM_modified %in% "67" ~ "60b", # going to pta. mercenario (middle poly)
    POEM_modified %in% "123" ~ "112aa", # going to pta. mercenario (poly furthest to shore)
    POEM_modified %in% "124" ~ "112ab", # going to pta. mercenario (poly furthes to shore)
    POEM_modified %in% "25" ~ "20aa", # moving line from north el choyudo to south el choyudo
    POEM_modified %in% "26" ~ "20ab",  # moving line from north el choyudo to south el choyudo
    TRUE ~ as.character(p_mod) # otherwise it cannot combine
  ))
```
